name: Ringo Broadcast Field Technician Vest
description:
Ringo's field broadcast technicians — the crew running cameras, signal repeaters, and live-feed rigs for everything from sponsored sports events to political press junkets — wear this vest as their standard on-site identifier. Built from a durable ripstop nylon in Ringo's electric red, the vest carries 14 external pockets of varying size calibrated for broadcast hardware: signal boosters, battery packs, lens filters, and interface cables all have designated homes. The Ringo 'R' logo in reflective white sits on the front and back, making crew identifiable in crowded or chaotic environments. Interior mesh lining keeps the vest breathable during long outdoor shoots.

The vest is designed to layer over personal clothing rather than replace it, which means it accommodates almost any body type or modification without manufacturer adjustment — the front closes with a wide-gap magnetic buckle system that clears most chest-mounted chrome, and the back panel is split to accommodate wing stubs or dorsal geneware modifications. A passive signal-routing harness built into the lining allows the wearer's BCI to interface directly with compatible Ringo broadcast hardware. Crew members have a complicated relationship with the vest: it marks you as essential on set, but it also makes you invisible to the talent and the executives who pretend the broadcast happens by itself.
cultural_context: In Ringo's world, the talent wears couture and the crew wears red vests. It's a deliberate hierarchy. But crew members who've been on enough shoots develop a kind of pride in the vest — they're the ones who actually make the broadcast work, and everyone in the industry knows it.
story_hooks: A field technician's vest contains broadcast footage auto-logged to Ringo's cloud servers from a shoot where something very wrong happened that never made it to air.
Someone in a Ringo vest is moving through a restricted Tier 4 event — but Ringo has no scheduled broadcast there, and the 'technician' doesn't appear on any crew manifest.
A veteran crew member discovers that the BCI signal-routing harness in her vest has been passively collecting biometric data from everyone she's been near on set for three years.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian sleeveless vest in electric red with high-visibility design language. Reads as 'working professional' on the street — instantly identifies the wearer as broadcast infrastructure, not talent. The silhouette is deliberately boxy and ungendered, built to layer over any torso configuration. Reflective Ringo 'R' logos front and back catch light in dim environments.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed, accommodation-focused. Cut wide through the torso with adjustable side panels and a split back panel. Designed to fit over muscle suit undergarments, dorsal implants, or chrome chest plating without binding. Magnetic front closure creates variable gap sizing — can be worn tight or deliberately loose to clear augmentations.
physical_description.primary_material: Industrial-grade ripstop nylon in electric red (Ringo brand signature). Lightweight but reinforced at stress points. Interior lined with breathable mesh for temperature regulation during extended outdoor shoots.
physical_description.texture: Smooth to slightly tactile ripstop surface with minimal sheen. Reinforced stitching visible at pocket corners and seams. Magnetic closures feel precise and industrial. Mesh lining visible through side vents has a fine, slightly clingy texture.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: electric red (Ringo corporate red). Accents: reflective white for logo and safety visibility. Minimal secondary colors — some models have charcoal mesh showing at vents.
physical_description.closures: Wide-gap magnetic buckle system (front center closure). Allows rapid on/off and accommodates non-standard chest geometry. No traditional buttons or zippers — all magnetic.
distinctive_features: 14 external pockets in graduated sizes, each calibrated for specific broadcast hardware (signal boosters, battery packs, lens filters, interface cables)
Reflective Ringo 'R' logo, front and back, 4-5 inches tall
Split rear panel extending 8 inches from neck to accommodate wings, dorsal fins, or back-mounted geneware
Passive signal-routing harness integrated into interior lining for BCI compatibility with Ringo broadcast gear
Interior mesh vents on both sides for airflow
Reinforced D-ring attachment points at shoulders and side seams (for hardware tethering)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 functional / corporate uniform. Signals employed infrastructure rather than wealth or status. Worn by people who make the broadcast system work.
physical_description.cultural_context: Ringo Data Services field crew uniform. Wearer is invisible to talent and executives, but essential to production. Signals technical competence and accessibility — you can approach this person to solve broadcast problems. Among crew, the vest carries pride and identity; it marks you as 'the people who actually know what's happening on set.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually well-maintained but visibly used. Pockets show wear from hardware insertion/removal. Possible dust, cable marks, or minor scuffs from field conditions. Never pristine, always functional. Some veteran crew members have small personalization marks or faded patches from long-term wear.
